attributes.body_ja:
「っぽい」または「ぽい」は、語（ご）のあとに付（つ）いてイ形容詞（けいようし）を作（つく）る接尾語（せつびご）です。どの「っぽい」にも「(A) の特徴（とくちょう）が感（かん）じられる」という意味（いみ）があります。具体的（ぐたいてき）には「(A) しがち」「(A) らしい」「(A) に見（み）える」のような意味（いみ）で使（つか）われます。また、多（おお）くの場合（ばあい）、「っぽい」は否定的（ひていてき）なニュアンスで使（つか）われます。

「っぽい」は、動詞（どうし）の連用形（れんようけい）や、そのほかの品詞（ひんし）の語幹（ごかん）につながります。

注意点（ちゅういてん）

「っぽい」が付（つ）いた語（ご）は、イ形容詞（けいようし）になるため、「っぽい」はふつうのイ形容詞（けいようし）と同（おな）じように活用（かつよう）します。

注意点（ちゅういてん）

「っぽい」の意味（いみ）は、それが付（つ）く語（ご）によって変（か）わります。基本的（きほんてき）な決（き）まりを見（み）てみましょう。

ここからわかるように、「っぽい」は実際（じっさい）の性質（せいしつ）ではなく、話（はな）し手（て）の感覚（かんかく）を表（あらわ）します。動詞（どうし）・形容詞（けいようし）・名詞（めいし）のどの場合（ばあい）でも、話（はな）し手（て）が「(A) の特徴（とくちょう）が強（つよ）く出（で）すぎている」と感（かん）じるときに使（つか）われます。そのため、しばしば否定的（ひていてき）なニュアンスを持（も）つことがあります。
attributes.body:
っぽい (occasionally also seen as ぽい) is a suffix that may be attached to many different types of words, in order to create new い-Adjectives. In all cases, っぽい indicates something that is 'exhibiting characteristics of (A)'. This is most often in reference to the way (A) is acting, or the way (A) looks. In English, っぽい may be translated as '(A)ish', '(A)like', or 'tendency to (A)'. っぽい quite often carries a negative connotation.

As っぽい creates い-Adjectives from other words, it may be used with the conjunctive form of verbs, or the 語幹（ごかん） (stem form) of any other word.

Caution

As っぽい creates new い-Adjectives, っぽい itself may be conjugated in exactly the same way as regular い-Adjectives.

Caution

The fundamental meaning of っぽい will change depending on what type of word it is being used with. The general rules are as follows:

Verb + っぽい - To have a tendency to do (A).

Adjective + っぽい - To exhibit all the signs of being (A).

Noun + っぽい - To obviously not be (A), although show signs of being (A).

From this, we can see that っぽい is generally based on the opinion of the speaker, rather than the innate qualities of what is being observed. Thus, with verbs, adjectives, and nouns, the speaker feels like (A) is in excess, compared to what would be expected. This 'being in excess of what is normal' in the opinion of the speaker is what creates the negative connotation.

attributes.body: Both がち and っぽい describe tendencies or characteristic qualities, but differ in nuance. がち is neutral and used for tendencies that happen often, e.g. つい忘れがちだ ('I tend to forget.'). っぽい expresses an inherent quality or the appearance of something, similar to the English '~ish', e.g. 子供っぽい性格 ('a childish personality').

attributes.body: Both ぎみ (often written in kanji as 気味) and っぽい describe tendencies or characteristics, but with different nuance. ぎみ suggests a slight or subtle tendency, often related to physical or emotional states, e.g. 疲れ気味 ('a bit tired') or 風邪気味 ('have a bit of a cold'). っぽい implies a more innate trait that gives the appearance or impression of something, e.g. 子どもっぽい ('childish') or 忘れっぽい ('forgetful').

attributes.body: Both っぽい and げ describe perceived qualities, but differ in nuance. っぽい refers to innate behaviors or traits that give a certain impression. For example, 子どもっぽい ('childish') or 怒りっぽい ('quick to anger'). In contrast, げ highlights perceived emotions in others. For example, 寂しげな顔 ('a lonely-looking face').

attributes.body: Both っぽい and そう express appearance or impression, but differ in nuance and usage. そう attaches to word stems and is neutral and often based on observation, e.g. 雨が降りそう ('It looks like it'll rain.'). っぽい is casual and attaches to nouns to mean '~ish' or '~like', e.g. 子供っぽい 'childish'. Unlike そう, it often carries a negative or demeaning tone.

attributes.body: Both ふりをする and っぽい describe imitation or resemblance, but with a key difference in nuance. ふりをする implies pretending to be or do something one is not, as in 知ったふりをする ('pretend to know'). In contrast, っぽい conveys a natural resemblance or tendency, often unconscious or inherent, as in 子供っぽい ('childish').

attributes.body: 的 and っぽい are similar in that both can be attached to nouns to turn them into adjectives (or adverbs, in the forms 的に and っぽく). They differ grammatically (的 functions as a な-adjective, while っぽい is an い-adjective), and in nuance. 的 has a wider range of uses, similar to English endings like '-al', '-ly', etc., e.g. 感情 'emotion' vs. 感情的 'emotional'. っぽい is narrower in use, and often carries a derogatory meaning, e.g. 子供っぽい 'childish'.

attributes.body: っぽい and らしい ① both describe being 'like' something, but with different nuances and formality. っぽい, similar to the English '-ish,' refers to having the characteristics of something without being that thing, and is very casual, e.g. 子どもっぽい態度 'childish behavior', e.g. from an adult. In contrast, らしい ① implies embodying a characteristic in a more fitting or expected way, e.g. 子どもらしい笑顔 'a smile just as you'd expect from a child'.
